entries.subject: fix(leaving-soon): page through every Maintainerr collection member
entries.notes: The C# file moved, it was not rewritten: upstream’s hunks to Services/LeavingSoonService.cs apply at Features/MediaTags/Services/LeavingSoonService.cs (the guard is Shared.Arr.ArrUrlGuard here) and are then changed. Kept from upstream: GetJsonAsync (one guarded GET: address guard, key header, 30-second timeout, no redirect followed, 16 MiB), the request GET /api/collections/media/{id}/content/{page}?size=500 for each active collection with a numeric id, at most 40 pages, the stop rule (page × 500 reaches totalSize, or a page without rows; a short page is not the last) and ParseCollections’ third parameter. Differences from upstream: (1) a failed page fails the refresh. Upstream catches every failure of a collection’s paging except a cancellation and falls back to the few embedded members without recording a failure, so one failed page takes the badge off the rest (on upstream’s build on the lab, 971 members: the second page of one collection answers HTTP 500 once and the status reads 353 items, no failure). Here only a 404 for a collection’s first page (a Maintainerr without the route) falls back to its embedded members; any other failure is the refresh’s failure, which keeps the previous answer and retries with the existing delays (the same run on the port: 971 items kept, last failure “HTTP 500”). (2) An answer of the paged route that is not an object with an items array is refused (“not a Maintainerr collections answer”); upstream reads it as a collection without members. (3) The paged members add to the embedded ones, they do not replace them: Maintainerr leaves a row out of a page when it cannot read that row’s metadata, so a member the list itself names stays one (on upstream’s build a page answered as {totalSize: 351, items: []} takes the badge off all 351 movies, the two the list embeds included; here those two keep it). (4) An id that is not a number: upstream calls TryGetInt32 on it, which throws for a string, so a list with such a collection fails the whole refresh (“request failed”) where the code before read its embedded members; here that collection is read from its embedded members and not asked for pages. totalSize has the same guard. (5) Only entries the parser recognises as collections are asked for pages, each id once, and the list’s unwrapping (data/items/collections/results) is one function for the parser and the paging, where upstream repeats it. (6) docs/enhanced/tags.md and docs/advanced/api.md describe the paged requests and their failure rule; upstream’s commit changes no docs. (7) Tests. Upstream’s commit has none and leaves its own LeavingSoonTests failing (9 of 47 at 53ebf043, run here: its fixture answers the collections list on every path, which the new code reads as a collection without members). Here the fixture gets the paged route (404 unless a test sets it) and three tests are added, all through RefreshAsync against the fixture server: 1,100 members over three pages with a short page, a collection answered without totalSize, an inactive one never asked for, ids that are missing or not numbers, the key and base path on every request; the pages adding to the embedded members, and the 404 fallback; twelve ways a page can fail or not be one, each keeping the last good answer with its reason and reaching no other host, a totalSize that is not a number, and a cancellation between pages. Two existing expectations change because a refresh now asks for pages too (the key test lists both requests; the redirect test’s “every request went to /api/collections” becomes a prefix check), and the fixture’s Requests counts the list requests, so the refresh-count assertions stand as they were. Kept from upstream as it is: members beyond 20,000 per collection are not read; a row that a page leaves out and the list does not embed is not a member; when a page comes back without rows, the members the list does not embed lose their badge until the next refresh. entries.subject: fix(hidden-content): saves keep changes made elsewhere and never replace a list that failed to load (#1056)
entries.notes: Upstream squashes the ten commits of its PR branch fix/hidden-content-saves. The first versions of five landed here first, as the rewrite's own commits, and are not repeated: 3d6c27f1 (a hidden list or shortcut list that failed to load stays null; Hidden Content refuses edits and never posts it; the shortcut editor stays read-only; the bootstrap and GET hidden-content.json / shortcuts.json read strictly, null / 500), f211f861 (each save reads the stored list and writes only this session's changes onto it; a Continue Watching / Next Up hide the server wrote is recorded as stored; saves run one at a time through enqueueWrite and flushPendingSave waits for a write in flight), 8518a722 (only the document's own pagehide stops the save retry, Status Tags and the settings panel), e38864fc (the Seerr card passes the plain title; names stored escaped read as plain text) and 92286fb2 (Manage Hidden Content opens the management dialog when the page is a tab or Plugin Page). Ported here is what upstream's versions changed since or add: (1) an edit refused because the list is not loaded says so (toast hidden_content_not_loaded, a new en.json string), confirmAndHide refuses before asking anything, and a settings panel switch whose change is refused goes back without running its side effects (dede014d); (2) the save's merge (model.ts withChanges): an entry the session read and changed or removed also reaches the server's copy of it under the other ID spelling, which the session never read, while keys the session read and left alone stay (fixup 9df8e43d and fb08398c): here an unhide right after Remove from Continue Watching left the entry the server stored under the dashed ID, so the item stayed out of Continue Watching; (3) a save with nothing of the session's to write posts nothing (upstream's first version); (4) each request of a save fails after 30 s, so a save that gets no answer is retried instead of holding later saves and a Continue Watching / Next Up removal, which is refused with its message (885e0198); (5) names stored HTML-escaped still read as plain text, but a save of other changes no longer rewrites them: the save merges onto the list as stored and the session reads names plain (model.ts withPlainNames); (6) refresh() keeps changes not saved yet on top of the list it reads; (7) the page's showPage() says whether it showed, and the Manage button uses that, so Plugin Pages chosen but not installed opens the page again (the rewrite opened the dialog) (0aefa637); (8) GET hidden-content.json, GET shortcuts.json and the bootstrap set content that does not parse aside to .corrupt-<ts> once, so the next read starts from the defaults (upstream's first version and e06003bd); here the strict read already holds the file's lock for the read and the move, leaves a file it could not open in place, and every save (shortcuts included) already takes that lock, so this is quarantineCorrupt on those three reads; the 500 messages are upstream's; (9) docs/enhanced/enhanced-features.md and docs/advanced/api.md applied with git apply, the bootstrap lines saying null as this tree's bootstrap writes it; the coverage-matrix row names this tree's tests. Tests: upstream's features-hidden-save.test.mjs and features-hidden-manage-button.test.mjs run against this tree's built modules in tests/frontend/features/hidden-content/, upstream's ApiUserDocumentReadTests is tests/backend/Features/Platform/ApiUserDocumentReadTests.cs, and its server-shape bootstrap test is in tests/frontend/bootstrap/bootstrap.test.mjs. On the branch's start 9 of the 33 frontend tests in the two new files fail (one per behaviour above) and 3 of the 19 backend tests in ApiUserDocumentReadTests and BootstrapContractTests; all pass after. Existing tests changed: BootstrapContractTests.UnreadableHiddenListAndShortcutsAreReportedAsFailedNotEmpty expected the unparseable files left in place and now expects them set aside once, then the defaults; seven Undo tests (HC-R4B-001 x3 in features-hidden-regressions, two in features-hidden-rewrite and two in tests/browser/hidden-content-rewrite.spec.cjs) undid a hide before any save and checked the POST, which (3) no longer sends, so each saves the hide first and checks the Undo's write. Differences from upstream: (a) a refused edit throws here after the message, as since 3d6c27f1 (its tests assert it), where upstream's returns false; for the user it is the same: the message, nothing asked, nothing saved. (b) This tree keeps one entry per item: an unhide removes every entry stored for the same item ID and a hide merges them (since its first version; 'GUID unhide removes equivalent storage aliases'). Upstream keeps a Continue Watching entry and a hide of the same item as separate entries, each removed on its own (fb08398c); its two tests for that are not ported, its server-shape test unhides a plain entry here, and this is filed for a decision (je12 found-bug NEW-20261113-135220). (3) Seerr's watchProviders are read as TMDB's shape with link and flatrate only, the parts the panel reads (upstream also copies rent, buy and ads, which nothing reads), and only two-capital-letter region codes. (4) The settings form, read fresh on every open here, keeps the Region of the document it read while Seerr's region is shown; upstream writes back its own copy of the saved Region (the same value).
